title: Boat and Helicopter Tourism
desc: Plan a small boat or helicopter tour offering with safe operations, licences, weather rules, guest care and pricing.
outcomes: Explain operator duties and passenger safety.
Compute cost per hour and per guest.
task: Plan a tour product with route, safety briefing, weather rules, licences, price and incident plan, working with licensed operators.
condition: A computer, a map, a spreadsheet, two peers and a licensed operator mentor. Learners do not operate vessels or aircraft.
standard: Licences and insurance are checked with sources; weather go/no-go rules are written; briefing covers equipment and emergencies; cost per guest is correct; peers rate Meets or better.
who: Tour planners, guides, hotel desks, port staff.
evidence: route plan, briefing script, go/no-go rules, price sheet
modules: Design a tour that guests will value and operators can run safely.
Duration, capacity, ports and landing sites.
A 45-minute coastal route with a sunset slot and a 20-minute boarding window.
Only licensed operators and crews run commercial trips.
Vessel or aircraft certificates, crew licences and operator permits.
A certificate expires next month; bookings after that date are stopped until renewal.
Clear numbers and a named decision maker.
Wind above a set limit cancels flights and guests are offered a new date or refund.
Guests must know what to do.
Life jackets, seat belts, exits and behaviour.
Guests repeat how to fasten a life jacket before boarding.
Man overboard, fire, engine failure and medical.
A drill finds the radio channel was wrong and the sheet is corrected.
Hourly cost of vessel or aircraft is high.
Cost per guest = hourly cost x hours / guests.
Hourly cost 40,000 INR for 8 guests is 5,000 INR each.
Routes avoid nesting sites in season.
The plan reaches 4.7 average guest score.
quiz: Who may operate?
Licensed operators and crew. (Covered in module 1: Product and route. To pass that module: Map and timings.)
Go/no-go factors?
Wind, visibility, waves or ceiling. (Covered in module 2: Licences and insurance. To pass that module: Sources and dates.)
Briefing items?
Equipment, exits, behaviour. (Covered in module 3: Weather and go/no-go. To pass that module: Numbers specified.)
Cost per guest?
Hourly cost x hours / guests. (Covered in module 4: Briefing and equipment. To pass that module: Under five minutes.)
Why drills?
Find weaknesses. (Covered in module 5: Emergencies. To pass that module: Steps ordered.)
Insurance for?
Passengers. (Covered in module 6: Cost and pricing. To pass that module: Currency shown.)
Why check expiry?
Valid permits. (Covered in module 7: Environment and community. To pass that module: Controls clear.)
Environment control?
Avoid nesting sites. (Covered in module 8: Operations plan. To pass that module: Complete.)
Cancel policy?
Refund. (Covered in module 8: Operations plan. To pass that module: Complete.)
What are checks logged?
Equipment inspection. (Covered in module 8: Operations plan. To pass that module: Complete.)
rubric: Every claim linked to a dated record and checked by a peer
Checked, dated and explained to others
next: tourism and hospitality, drone operations, customer service.
local: Maritime and aviation law differ by place.
ladder: Product and route

L1: learner can name tour types. Focus module: Product and route (Understand, 3 h). Design the experience. Key points: Scenic, sunset, wildlife, transfer. Duration, capacity, ports and landing sites. Accessibility.

Teach: open with the worked example. A 45-minute coastal route. Then set the activity: Design a route. Mark against the standard: Map and timings. Check at this level: Who may operate? Model answer: Licensed operators and crew. Types.
Licences and insurance

L2: learner knows licence basics. Focus module: Licences and insurance (Apply, 5 h). Only licensed operators. Key points: Vessel or aircraft certificates, crew licences, operator permits. Insurance for passengers. Check expiry dates.

Teach: open with the worked example. A certificate expires next month; booking stops. Then set the activity: Make a checklist. Mark against the standard: Sources and dates. Check at this level: Go/no-go factors? Model answer: Wind, visibility, waves or ceiling. Licences.
Weather and go/no-go

L3: learner can read weather rules. Focus module: Weather and go/no-go (Apply, 5 h). Safety over schedule. Key points: Wind, visibility, waves, ceiling. Clear numbers and a decision maker. Refund policy for cancellations.

Teach: open with the worked example. Wind above a set limit cancels flights. Then set the activity: Write rules. Mark against the standard: Numbers specified. Check at this level: Briefing items? Model answer: Equipment, exits, behaviour. Weather.
Briefing and equipment

L4: learner can brief guests. Focus module: Briefing and equipment (Apply, 4 h). Guests must know what to do. Key points: Life jackets, seat belts, exits, behaviour. Language options; check understanding. Equipment inspection log.

Teach: open with the worked example. Guests repeat how to fasten a life jacket. Then set the activity: Write a briefing script. Mark against the standard: Under five minutes. Check at this level: Cost per guest? Model answer: Hourly cost x hours / guests. Brief.
Emergencies
L5: learner can price. Focus module: Emergencies (Evaluate, 4 h). Plan and drill. Key points: Man overboard, fire, engine failure, medical. Contacts and roles. Practice drills.

Teach: open with the worked example. A drill finds the radio channel was wrong. Then set the activity: Write a plan. Mark against the standard: Steps ordered. Check at this level: Why drills? Model answer: Find weaknesses. Price.
Environment and community
L6: learner can lead. Focus module: Environment and community (Evaluate, 3 h). Be a good neighbour. Key points: Noise, wildlife, emissions. Flight paths and speed rules. Local jobs.

Teach: open with the worked example. Routes avoid nesting sites. Then set the activity: List controls. Mark against the standard: Controls clear. Check at this level: Insurance for? Model answer: Passengers. Lead.
Operations plan
L7: learner can audit. Focus module: Operations plan (Create, 3 h). Write and present. Key points: Roles, schedule, records. Review each season. Guest feedback.

Teach: open with the worked example. The plan reaches 4.7 average score. Then set the activity: Present. Mark against the standard: Complete. Check at this level: Why check expiry? Model answer: Valid permits. Peer audit.
